title: Demo sprint
summary: A short two-day sprint at Workkit to try out the platform: a guided warm-up, one bug, two small features and a requirement that changes halfway.

tickets.title: Add yourself to the team in the README
tickets.description:
Welcome to the team! Before the real work starts, one small ticket to learn how we work here. Every ticket has a key: WK stands for Workkit, and 0 is the number of this ticket. Put the key in your branch name and in the title of your pull request, so the board can follow your work.

Add a Team section at the end of README.md with your name and your role. The board guides you through every step.
acceptance_criteria: README.md ends with a section called Team
The section lists your name and your role, developer
The change is merged through a pull request with WK-0 in its title
tickets.review_notes: This is the user's very first pull request on a guided warm-up ticket. Approve it when README.md ends with a Team section that lists their name and the role developer; small differences in format are fine. A change to README.md alone needs no test. Keep the review short and warm: one sentence on what went well. Only ask for a change when the Team section is missing or does not contain a name.

tickets.title: A lease request can be approved twice
tickets.description:
Sales reported that a few lease requests ended up with two contracts for the same laptop. The approver says they only clicked once, but the approve button stays active for a moment and the request seems to go through twice when the page is slow.

Please find out why this can happen and make sure a request can only ever be approved once.
acceptance_criteria: A lease request that is already approved cannot be approved again
Approving the same request twice never creates a second contract
A test covers the double approval

tickets.title: Filter the catalogue by monthly budget
tickets.description: Employees browse the catalogue of laptops and smartphones, but they think in monthly amounts, not in purchase prices. Several customers asked if they can enter the amount they want to spend per month and only see devices they can lease for that amount.
acceptance_criteria: The catalogue has a filter for the maximum monthly price
Only devices that can be leased for that amount or less are shown
An empty filter shows the whole catalogue
The filter is part of the URL so a filtered list can be shared

tickets.title: Show the repair status to the employee
tickets.description: When a leased device is broken, the employee reports it and Repairs takes it in. Right now the employee has no idea what is going on after that and phones HR. Claire from the customer's HR team would like the employee to see the status of the repair on the device page.
acceptance_criteria: The device page shows the current repair status when there is an open repair
The employee sees the date of the last status change
A device without an open repair shows no repair section

events.body: Hi {first_name}, welcome to the Workkit team! I'm Sarah, the team lead. Take your time to get familiar with the codebase. If something is unclear, just ask. Daniel will walk you through today's tickets in a minute.

Hey {first_name}, Daniel here, I'm the project manager. Start with WK-0, a small warm-up: the board walks you through every step. After that, two tickets for you today: WK-1 is a bug Sales keeps running into, WK-2 is a small feature customers have been asking for. Open a pull request when you think a ticket is ready and Sarah will have a look.

Sorry {first_name}, a small change on WK-2: I just talked to Sales and they want to use the same filter to find devices that are for sale. I added it to the acceptance criteria. Can you take it into account?
add_criteria: The filter can also be limited to devices that are for sale

events.body: Good morning {first_name}! Day two. Today there is one ticket, WK-3. Claire from the customer's HR team has asked for it twice already, so she is looking forward to this one.
WK-3 is merged, nice work. Employees will phone HR a lot less now.
That's the sprint wrapped up, {first_name}. Thanks for the work these two days. Have a look back at your pull requests and see what you would do differently next time.
